rationale: The Court will likely reject the Eighth Circuit’s education-specific “bad faith or gross misjudgment” requirement as textually untethered and inconsistent with uniform-meaning principles, while emphasizing that compensatory damages under Title II/§504 require intentional discrimination (often deliberate indifference) under Barnes/Gebser/Davis. Roberts is best positioned to write a narrow, administrability-conscious majority, with Alito likely dissenting to preserve the heightened screen and one or more textualist concurrences (Thomas/Barrett/Gorsuch) possible to stress statutory coherence and limits on judicially created carveouts.
